test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: Let p, q, r and s be positive natural numbers having three exact factors including 1 and the number itself. If q > p and both are two-digit numbers, and r > s and both are one-digit numbers, then the value of the expression (p-q-1)/(r-s) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers with exactly 3 factors are squares of prime numbers (P²).

One-digit squares of primes: 4 and 9. Since r > s, s = 4 and r = 9.

Two-digit squares of primes: 25 and 49. Since q > p, p = 25 and q = 49.

Expression = (p − q − 1) ÷ (r − s) = (25 − 49 − 1) ÷ (9 − 4) = −25 ÷ 5 = −5.

Check options: −s − 1 = −4 − 1 = −5. This matches.

**∴ The correct answer is −s − 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

p, q, r, s have 3 factors each. q > p (2 digits), r > s (1 digit).

**Formula Used:**

If a number N = aⁿ, where a is prime, the number of factors is (n + 1). For 3 factors, n + 1 = 3 ⇒ n = 2. Thus, the numbers must be squares of prime numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc4280ba5a22451b899cd66d5578b904b1ee0a75c0729e223fbc9c3651f165c5.png] 

Identifying the values:

⇒ Prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11...

⇒ Squares are 4, 9, 25, 49, 121...

⇒ For one-digit numbers r > s: r = 9, s = 4.

⇒ For two-digit numbers q > p: q = 49, p = 25.

Calculation of the expression:

⇒ (p − q − 1) ÷ (r − s)

⇒ (25 − 49 − 1) ÷ (9 − 4)

⇒ (−24 − 1) ÷ 5

⇒ −25 ÷ 5 = −5

Verifying with Option (1):

⇒ −s − 1 = −4 − 1 = −5

**∴ The correct answer is −s − 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Factors of a Square Number

A number has an odd number of factors if and only if it is a perfect square. A number has exactly 3 factors if it is the square of a prime number.

Number of Factors Formula

For N = p₁a × p₂b, the number of factors is (a + 1)(b + 1). For N to have 3 factors, (a + 1) must be 3, implying a = 2 for a single prime base.

Prime Squares Identification

Common prime squares are 4 (2²), 9 (3²), 25 (5²), 49 (7²), 121 (11²), 169 (13²), etc.</p
